annotations.text:
THREE DIRECTIONS, ONE PALETTE

Every prototype is 390 × 844 — a real iPhone, not a desktop layout shrunk. All three share the locked palette, Instrument Serif for titles and hero numerals, Manrope for UI, and the same four-tab bottom bar. So what you are choosing is LAYOUT AND DENSITY, not colour or type.

What is fixed in all three: no horizontal scroll, 44px minimum tap targets, 13px minimum body text, filter rows that scroll inside their own track instead of widening the page.

A — COMMAND
Most information per screen. The oldest lead is a hero card with its reply button; everything behind it is a compact row carrying name, reason, age and class icon.

Best if you want to see the whole queue at a glance and triage in one scroll.
Tradeoff: the busiest of the three. On a bad day it is a lot of red at once.

B — FOCUS
One lead fills the screen, reply box included, so there is nothing between opening the app and sending. Everyone else collapses to a single strip of ages you tap to expand.

Best if the queue is usually short and the job is 'answer the oldest one, now'.
Tradeoff: you cannot see the queue's shape without a second tap. Leads is grouped by what you would act on rather than sorted.

C — ATLAS
Editorial. Serif carries the counts and the names, the pressure bar is typographic rather than a widget, and the leads list is a rule-separated index instead of cards.

Best if you want it to feel like a considered product rather than an admin tool — the one to show an agency.
Tradeoff: the least dense. Fewer leads visible before scrolling.
